sentences.text: Cetiosaurus was a quadrupedal herbivore featuring a long neck, a small head, relatively long forelimbs, and a shorter tail compared to most sauropods.
This animal is estimated to have reached a length of about 16 meters and a weight of roughly 11 tonnes.
The Rutland specimen is about 40% complete and adds significantly to the known skeletal elements, particularly in the neck.
The skull is largely unknown, except possibly for the brain case found in specimen OUMNH J13596.
Cetiosaurus was named in 1842, becoming the first sauropod genus described from bones.
The genus name was chosen by Sir Richard Owen because he initially believed the animal was a large marine crocodile rather than a land-dwelling dinosaur.
Cetiosaurus oxoniensis was officially designated the type species of the genus in 2014.
The C. oxoniensis specimen at Leicester Museum and Art Gallery is 15 meters long and includes fourteen cervical, ten dorsal, five sacral, and about fifty caudal vertebrae.
Paul considered Cetiosaurus a feeding generalist that ate at both low and medium-high levels due to its moderately long neck and limb proportions.
The name Cetiosaurus means 'whale lizard', derived from Greek words for 'sea monster' and 'lizard'.
In 1905, Arthur Smith Woodward placed C. leedsi in Cetiosaurus, including a partial sauropod skeleton from the Oxford Clay of Peterborough.
The holotype of C. leedsi is now considered indeterminate eusauropod remains, while the Peterborough skeleton is assigned to the valid species Cetiosauriscus stewarti.
Upchurch and Martin suggested changing the type species to C. oxoniensis to stabilize the classification of Cetiosaurus.
Cetiosaurus fossils date to the Middle Jurassic period, specifically the Bajocian to Bathonian ages.
Cetiosaurus lived approximately 171 to 165 million years ago in what is now Britain and possibly France.
It shared its territory with predators like Megalosaurus and Eustreptospondylus in an environment of floodplains and open woodlands.

It is debated whether two tail vertebrae recorded by Lydekker in 1888 as originating from the Blisworth skeleton actually exist in the Natural History Museum collections, as they could not be located in a 2003 study.
Duriatitan humerocristatus is often considered a nomen dubium.
If C. brevis were the type species, it would cause taxonomic instability because Pelorosaurus is recognized as a different kind of sauropod.
